subject: RE: Renewal negotiation — Cobalt Health request for concessions
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobalthealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Anu Roy <anu.roy@cobalthealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion — next steps and asks

Priya,

Hope you’re well — our renewal for Q1 2027 is coming up and I wanted to flag that we’re in a tough planning window. Several of our product launches have been delayed and hiring is frozen for the quarter, so our consumption is down ~40% vs plan. Finance is pressing us for savings and I need to present a reasonable path to keep Redwood as our inference partner.

Specific asks from our side:
- One-time renewal credit against next invoice (we were targeting ~25% given current utilization).
- A term reset (push the renewal anniversary 3 months) so we can align to GTM timing.
- A temporary SLA add-on or elevated uptime commitment while we onboard new workloads (we want to avoid production risk during ramp).

I know these are non-standard asks — if there’s an executive path to approve concessions for renewal saves, please escalate. If not, point me to the right person and I’ll work with procurement. We’d prefer an agreement by mid-November so procurement can process the PO.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call.

Samir
Samir Patel
VP Engineering, Cobalt Health
samir.patel@cobalthealth.com
(415) 555-0192

Attachments: renewal_calendar_v2.pdf (calendar of internal approvals)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cobalthealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — next steps and asks

Samir — thanks for the context and the heads up. I’m sorry to hear the timing is tight. We value Cobalt Health a lot and I want to keep you on a path that preserves product access while being responsible to our margin.

I need to escalate this to our deal desk and finance for executive approval on any one-time credits or term adjustments. To make the ask as crisp as possible, could you confirm:
- Current ARR and renewal ARR (rough numbers are fine)
- Desired PO/commitment timing (you mentioned mid-Nov)
- If you’d accept a shorter-term SLA trial (6 months) rather than a permanent SLA change

I’ll pull together a one-page summary and route it to our revenue leader and GC if we need a term reset. I’ll also attach the SOC2 excerpt and a redline SOW for their review.

If you’re available, I can do a 20-minute call today or tomorrow to align.

— Priya

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: FWD: Renewal discussion — Cobalt Health (need approval)

Team — forwarding Samir’s renewal ask. Quick summary and proposal below. Need an approval path by EOD 10-Nov so we can respond before their procurement freeze.

Account: Cobalt Health (HS-43129)
Current ARR: ~$420k
Renewal target: $430k (annual)
Contract type: standard Hosted API + Dedicated capacity pilot (50% discount pilot originally)
Renewal timeline: PO expected by 15-Nov ideally

Customer asks: 25% one-time credit; 3-month term reset; elevated SLA or temporary higher uptime guarantee while they ramp workloads

My recommended concession (minimal to save deal):
- One-time credit = 20% of renewal invoice (~$86k) applied to next invoice
- Term reset = 3 months (push anniversary) instead of 6-month reset request
- SLA add-on = 6-month trial of our 99.9% SLA (no permanent change to contract; include rollback clause and usage review at 60 days)

Why: preserves revenue, limits permanent SLO exposure, gives them runway to align GTM, and buys us time to drive usage back up.

Impact: finance estimate of margin hit ~12% on the renewal (pending final numbers).

Attachments I’m sending to the customer pending approval: Cobalt_HEALTH_Renewal_Redline_SOW.pdf, renewal_summary_Cobalt.xlsx, SOC2_extract.pdf

Ask: Rishi — can you approve the above concession (20% credit + 3-month reset + 6-month SLA trial) or do you need the deeper concession (25% credit + 3-month reset)? Laura — please confirm CS availability for 60-day usage review and implementation of the SLA trial if approved. Marissa — FYI on exec comms / discount cap.

Thanks,
Priya

Subject: Re: FWD: Renewal discussion — Cobalt Health (need approval)

Priya — thanks for the clear ask and the numbers. Approve the limited concession below:

- One-time credit: 20% of renewal invoice (~$86k)
- Term reset: 3 months (push anniversary)
- SLA: 6-month trial of 99.9% with documented rollback and a usage & performance review at 60 days

Conditions:
1) Customer must sign an updated SOW and DocuSign envelope within 7 business days of offer acceptance.
2) Include a commitment to a joint usage review at day 60; if usage hasn’t recovered by >15%, case to be escalated for commercial review.
3) Finance to confirm final margin impact; if the margin hit >15% we re-open approvals.

Laura — please coordinate CS to schedule the SLA onboarding and the day-60 review. Marissa — please log the concession in our deal desk tracker and mark as exec-approved (Rishi).

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

- One-time credit: 20% applied to your next renewal invoice (approx. $86k)

Conditions: signed updated SOW via DocuSign within 7 business days; joint usage review at day 60 to confirm ramp; standard rollback clause applies. I’ve attached the redlined SOW and a short renewal summary for your procurement team.

DocuSign: https://na2.docusign.net/ENVELOPE/0AB12345

Thank you — looking forward to keeping Cobalt Health on Redwood.
